title: How Sauter-Finegan ended and the State Department tour
summary: The band disbanded over taxes and losses and was passed over for State Department tours.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Then as it right after the band disbanded?

A couple of years; we disbanded--the government was threatening to take all the money at the gate to pay the taxes we owed them, and that would have left us stranded who knows where, and we were constantly being sent out on the road, at a loss. We never made any money with that thing, not enough to keep the thing going.
Toward the end of it, they were being to have State Department tours and we thought that that would be just a great thing
Yeah, Dizzy's band did one and Woody's band.
We got the message that they thought we were not representatively American. They didn't want to send us abroad. Another person said--
Who is the idiot who made that decision?
Some critic, a very famous one, who was on the board.

I don't want to say. But it was also suggested that maybe it was too expensive, because we didn't have a huge percussion section, but I don't see how that could have been. They could send a lot of percussion too.
They could send symphony orchestras abroad.
So I have a sneaky suspicion it was knocked out by the critics.

Anyway, we decided to stop it for a while and tell our agents not until you can book us in such a way that we can come out at least being even, and that was the end of the band. It never went out again.
Unless you could grab and somehow influence the thinking of the time, it was wrong, because right after that, rock shot up.
